if you are contacted by Jobcentre Plus, you should where possible, return any evidence or contribution within the stated timescales, or if a deadline has not been stated within a maximum of 5 working days

if your Participant remains dissatisfied at this point, they will be advised to approach you directly about any issues which relate to the service you provide

4. Participant makes a complaint to you about Confident Futures policy. If a Participant raises a complaint with you regarding participation in Confident Futures or any other issue relating to Confident Futures policy, you should direct them to contact the Jobcentre Plus team dealing with their case to try to resolve the issue.

5. An employer makes a complaint about you regarding the Confident Futures.

During the life of the contract an employer, with whom you have placed or attempted to place a Participant, may wish to raise a complaint about you:

on receipt of the complaint, you should follow your procedure as normal

you must deal with the employer’s complaint in the same way as you would any complaint made against you

6. An elected member of a national or international body makes a complaint to you on behalf of your Participant There may be occasions when an elected member of a national or international body would write to you on behalf of your Participant, for example:

Member of Parliament (MP)

Member of the National Assembly for Wales (AM)

These representatives do have the authority to act on behalf of your Participant, but where you have any doubt about responding to the elected member, you can ask for confirmation that they are acting on behalf of your Participant.

If the elected member came to DWP on behalf of your Participant with feedback that involved both DWP and yourself, DWP will co-ordinate a joint response by getting a contribution from you.

7. Participant wishes to make a complaint about DWP or Jobcentre Plus

The Participant is advised to follow DWP’s complaints procedure .

Independent Case Examiner (ICE) role and processes

6.38 The ICE Office provides an impartial resolution and investigation service for people who are unhappy with the way their complaint has been dealt with.

6.39 ICE have 2 primary objectives:

to act as an independent adjudicator if your Participant considers that they have not been treated fairly or have not had their complaints dealt with in a satisfactory manner

to support service improvements by providing constructive comment and meaningful systemic recommendations

Who can raise a complaint to ICE?

6.40 Participants who are unhappy with the way in which their complaint has been dealt with by either DWP or their contracted service providers.

6.41 To raise a complaint with ICE the Participant must meet the following criteria:

have given you or DWP the opportunity to respond and resolve the issue

have received the final response, that explained that they can take their complaint to ICE if they are not satisfied with the response they have received

raise the complaint with ICE within 6 months of receiving the final response from yourself or DWP

Note: ICE will only accept complaints for investigation if they meet all 3 of these criteria.

What happens when a case is raised with ICE?

6.42 After they accept a complaint, ICE will contact you to confirm that each step of your internal process has been completed. If they feel that you have not completed your process satisfactorily you may be asked to revisit some steps to seek resolution before ICE are prepared to investigate further.

Note: ICE will generally only consider a complaint after your own complaints process has been completed and a final response has been issued. If internal complaint stages have not been exhausted, ICE may not investigate.

6.43 You must deal with any correspondence of any nature from ICE within the stated timescales and at least within 5 working days.

6.44 Once ICE has accepted a case, they will work to resolve the case by taking the following 3 stage approach, attempting to resolve matters at the earliest possible stage. At every stage, you will have the opportunity to give your version of events and offer any supporting evidence.

6.45 See the Complaint resolution core briefing pack: DWP provider guidance and refer to stage 1 Resolution, Stage 2 Settlement and Stage 3 Investigation Report in Chapter 4: ICE.

The Public Service Ombudsman (PSO)

6.46 Participants have no right of appeal against ICE’s decision. However, if your Participant is unhappy with the outcome of the ICE investigation, they can ask their MP to refer their case to the PSO. If the PSO accepts their case and upholds the complaint they may recommend additional remedies including financial redress for your Participant, which you would also be liable to pay. For more information, visit the PSO website.

Fraud prevention

6.47 If you suspect that your Participant is committing fraud you should follow the procedures outlined on Report benefit fraud.

6.48 DWP places the utmost importance on the need to prevent fraud and irregularity in the delivery of its contracts. You are required to, as a minimum, adhere to the following 4 principles:

have an established system that enables your staff to report inappropriate behaviour by colleagues in respect of any claims for payment in relation to Confident Futures contract

fee is an amount payable by DWP to you monthly, starting from the first month of the contract going live up to a maximum of 20 months. For further information, refer to the Delivery Fee Payments section of your Restart Contract Terms and Conditions

5.2 If your Customer Service Standard performance falls below the agreed standards, this will be discussed with your Performance Manager during performance reviews and improvement action agreed as part of the Performance Management Intervention Regime.

Funding model

5.3 There are 2 distinct elements to the Confident Futures funding model:

Delivery Fee

Output Payment

Delivery Fee Payment

5.4 Delivery Fee will constitute 80% of the total contract value. You will not need to submit claims for Delivery Fee payments. The Delivery Fee will be automatically paid to you monthly in arrears from month one of the contract going live, up to and including month 20.

Output Payment

5.5 Output payments are capped at 20% of the total contract value. You will only be paid an Output Payment when DWP has confirmed that the qualifying conditions described in the Confident Futures Specification and later in this section have been met.

Qualifying conditions for Output Payments

5.6 Output payments are only payable where the agreed Output has been completed in accordance with the requirements set out in the Specification (Annex 8: Submission Timings and Acceptance Criteria) and submitted within the required timescales.

5.7 Providers must submit completed Outputs within the timescales set out in the Specification (Annex 8 Submission Timings and Acceptance Criteria) and Chapter 9: Confident Futures Contract Metrics, Managing Performance and Risk Assurance of this Guidance. The Authority will review all submitted Outputs and, where an Output does not meet the required standards or further information is required, may request that the provider rework and resubmit the Output. Outputs submitted outside the required timescales, or which do not meet the required quality standards, are incomplete, or are not supported by sufficient evidence following any rework and resubmission request, will be deemed ineligible for payment.

5.8 All submissions will be assessed by the Authority, and payment will only be made where the qualifying conditions have been met.

Payments to providers

5.9 All payments will be made through the appropriate IT system or PRaP in line with the amounts set out in the contract. Note that DWP can only make direct payments to UK bank accounts.

5.10 When shipping Management information (MI) lines these will appear as outcome payments of £0.01 each, note these payments will be made on the next working day. Details of these payments are described in Chapter 8: Using the Provider Referral and Payment (PRaP) System for Confident Futures in the MI lines.

VAT

5.11 Your VAT obligations are covered in the Terms and Conditions of the contract.

Additional VAT Requirements for Self-billing Contracts

5.12 The following guidance should be read in conjunction with the HMRC guidance VAT Notice 700/62: Self-Billing.

5.13 HMRC guidance states that under a self-billing contract both parties are responsible for ensuring that the VAT is charged correctly on invoices. As part of your bid, you were asked to provide the VAT rate or rates that should be charged for each part of the funding model.

Note: You will be asked to confirm that the VAT rate or rates quoted as part of your bid are still correct prior to commencement date of the contract. The onus is on you to provide the VAT rate for this contract as per HMRC guidelines. DWP will however, assist in this matter by providing an annual self-billing contract and requesting confirmation of the VAT rate or rates. If the self-billing agreement process is delayed for any reason, you are still responsible for notifying the VAT rate or rates to the Authority on an annual basis.

DWP’s responsibilities

5.14 DWP is responsible for ensuring that:

VAT rates are sent to the provider

an annual self-billing agreement is in place; and VAT rate or rates are changed on the PRaP system if you notify a change in your VAT status

5.15 DWP will seek agreement from you to the self-billing arrangement on an annual basis and request that you confirm the VAT rate or rates to be applied to all aspects of the funding model.

Provider’s responsibilities

5.16 You are responsible for:

providing a signed self-billing agreement promptly on an annual basis when requested by DWP

ensuring that DWP is immediately notified of a change in the VAT rate(s) should they change during an agreement term

ensuring that duplicate invoices are not sent to DWP for a supply which is self-billed

ensuring that you fully understand and comply with VAT Notice 700/62

Chapter 6: Health and safety, accidents, unacceptable behaviour, fraud prevention and complaints

6.1 This chapter pulls together various key pieces of information that you will need to be aware of in respect of working with your Participants and also details what you must have in place to ensure Participants who are unhappy with the service they receive are able to raise a confidential complaint, and the processes you must follow to respond and resolve any issues raised.

Health and safety

6.2 All Participants on Confident Futures are entitled to train and work in a healthy and safe environment with due regard to their welfare. Under Health and Safety Law they are regarded as your employees, whether they are paid by you or not. You must, therefore, comply with your Duty of Care under the Health and Safety at Work Act 1974 and the Act’s associated regulations in the same way as you would do for any other member of your workforce.

6.3 You must ensure that your Participants receive appropriate health and safety induction, training and supervision, and that systems are in place for checking this, both within your own organisation and at any of your supply chain partners.

l, you may wish to request that your Participant is excluded from your premises. The situation must be one of genuine risk to staff and not just because your Participant is difficult, and you must supply evidence about why exclusion is appropriate.

6.17 If exclusion is sought, a request should be made via your Performance Manager who will forward the details to the PTWA for a decision to be made based on the individual circumstances.

6.18 Participants will not be excluded based on potentially violent or inappropriate behaviour (for example, racial or sexual verbal assault, foul language or the issuing of threats, or if your Participant refuses to engage). However, you must show a duty of care to your Participants and staff and in certain circumstances the only immediate option may be to temporarily remove your Participant from the situation.

6.19 In some circumstances your Participants who have a Keep Customer Interactions Safe (KCIS) safety measure marker recorded against them may be considered as posing a risk to the health and safety of staff. These Participants will be subjected to certain control measures to ensure staff safety. Further information on your Participant’s KCIS safety measure marker can be requested by contacting the Jobcentre Plus SPoC.

6.20 Examples of behaviours that would result in control measures being implemented would be where a Participant:

has committed an actual physical assault on a member of staff or another Participant, regardless of injury

has committed an actual physical assault on a member of staff’s family

has attempted to commit a physical assault on a member of staff or another Participant

stalked a member of staff or another Participant (which is defined as “the wilful, malicious and repeated following and harassing of another person”)

suffers from a severe mental illness, and a qualified medical practitioner or social worker states that they are likely to pose a danger to staff

has made a threat of violence either face to face, over the phone, or in writing

has displayed threatening or aggressive behaviour

6.21 Where incidents such as this occur or where control measures have been introduced by Jobcentre Plus then you may decide how best you can handle your Participant, suggested controls include:

holding interviews in public areas

having a colleague present at interviews

informing senior staff or managers of interview details

Fast Track Incidents

6.22 While all incidents of unacceptable Participant behaviour are serious, some may have to be afforded a particular importance and dealt with as a priority because of their nature and circumstances.

6.23 When notifying DWP of an incident you should complete the UCCF02 form and select urgent 2-way call and send to the appropriate designated Jobcentre Inbox. You should then contact your Jobcentre Plus SPoC and advise that you have submitted the form and require an urgent call if an incident occurs that can be defined as a ‘serious’ or ‘fast track’ incident.

Note: Where the Participant is no longer claiming Universal Credit, you are not required to submit the UCCF02 notification form you should follow your own internal processes. Should you require any support in deciding on the right course of action contact your Performance Manager.

6.24 A serious incident is an incident which compromises the health and safety of DWP staff or the staff of our supply chain partners, or our ability to safely use our premises. The serious nature or sensitivity of the incident warrants an immediate notification to senior management, prior to further investigation.

Note: This also applies when the Participant is on work experience or periods of attachment to an employer, in addition to time spent with yourself or supply chain partners.

6.25 Sometimes a serious incident may not neatly fit within the criteria below (this list is not exhaustive):

actual assault (intentional physical contact) has occurred - which is directed at DWP or partner employees in connection with their duties

weapon, or other item presenting a similar level of threat, has been used to harm, attempt to harm or intimidate

is significant disruption to normal business

is a significant cost implication (such as, estimated at over £2,000) for your business, DWP or your supply chain partners’ business, for example, damage to property

has been a viable targeted or personalised threat (and police advice has been sought)

suicide, attempted suicide or self-harm incident, understood to be directly connected to DWP business

6.26 Incidents occurring on either your own, your supply chain, co-located premises, or in your Participants home may need to be Fast Tracked. If this is the case, you should submit the UCCF02 notification form and alert your Jobcentre Plus SPoC immediately via telephone, who will raise the incident on your behalf. You should also make your Performance Manager aware, as soon as possible. If you are unclear as to whether an incident should be considered a Fast Track, you should contact your Performance Manager for further advice and support.

Overview of Incident Referral Process

6.27 Outlined below is the process you should follow to manage Participant behaviour following an incident.

1. Report the incident

complete the UCCF02 form and select urgent 2-way call and send to the appropriate designated Jobcentre In box

you should then contact your Jobcentre Plus SPoC and advise that you have submitted the form and require an urgent call

2. Attempt to manage the Participant’s behaviour

take appropriate steps to address and manage the behaviour

3. Determine whether the incident has been resolved

if yes, no further action is required

if no, continue to Step 4

4. Consider whether the Participant has consistently ignored attempts to resolve the issue

if no, continue to manage the Participant’s behaviour and make further attempts to resolve the issue

if yes, continue to Step 5
